newsitem.title: UK: EURO OIL SWAPS WEAK, MOGAS DOWN $2.5, FUEL DOWN $1.
newsitem.headline: EURO OIL SWAPS WEAK, MOGAS DOWN $2.5, FUEL DOWN $1.

text.p: European oil swaps slipped lower on Monday as gasoline fell a further $2.50 a tonne and fuel finally eased $1 after holding steady for much of last week.
The resumption of Iraqi oil exports continued to dominate the market but Brent crude futures nudged a few cents higher and short-dated CFD swaps were unchanged.
"You would expect to see the cracks weaken this week," said a trader referring to big refinery margins in the West.
Gas oil crack spreads against Brent talked $4.45 a barrel for the fourth quarter having recently been heavily sold by the trade around $4.60, said brokers.
The four quarters next year were valued at $4.40 a barrel, $3.95, $4.45 and $5.15 respectively.
Swaps for physical were little changed around $6 a tonne above the IPE for September EN590, rising to $9.50 in the fourth quarter.
Gasoline slipped around $2.50 a tonne in outright values but was steady on crack spreads against Brent.
The four quarters next year were pegged around $3.50 a barrel, $4.75, $4.30 and $3.50 respectively.
Naphtha fell $1 a tonne but talk held steady on crack spreads.
Heavy fuel fell $1 a tonne to $93.50 for August and September barges. Thereafter, prices nudge $1 a tonne higher each month until a peak in February around $99.
Low sulphur held narrow premiums above barges amid poor demand from Italy and good supply.
Brent CFDs were unchanged from last Friday. This week's dates held 38 cents under October with next week at 34 cents under followed by two weeks at 32 cents under. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 4984
